newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RINGGIT SLIPS ON BULLISH DOLLAR SENTIMENT.
newsitem.headline: RINGGIT SLIPS ON BULLISH DOLLAR SENTIMENT.

text.p: * Ringgit slips on bullish dollar sentiment
* Local and offshore buying of dollar from 2.6440
* Dollar/ringgit seen testing initial target of 2.6500
* Trading cautious after Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's remark about ringgit
The ringgit remained weak in early Asian trading on the back of the dollar's bullish sentiment, dealers said.
"Dollar/ringgit remains very biddish," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore. "People are not really buying aggressively but the bids are getting higher."
He said the weaker ringgit reflected the dollar's worldwide strength, adding that local and offshore players were buying dollar/ringgit from 2.6440.
At 0215 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6465/85 to a dollar, against its 2.6455/85 close in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
The ringgit hit a low of 2.6490 late on Thursday on a fresh wave of selling triggered by rumours the governor of central Bank Negara Malaysia has resigned.
A Bank Negara spokesman on Thursday denied that Ahmad Mohamed Don has stepped down.

Dealers said they expected the dollar to test its initial target of 2.6500 later in the day, ahead of its recent high of 2.6530. "A break of the 2.6500 level will take it to 2.66 very quickly," said the European bank dealer.
Dealers said trading was cautious following Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's remark that he was concerned with the sharp fall in the ringgit.
However, he declined to give the ringgit's level where the government would consider comfortable.
Mahathir told reporters on Thursday that the recent restriction on swaps would remain as long as necessary.

Bank Negara ordered local banks to limit non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday, as part of an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit and bring down interest rates.
